bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash in hand moved from ₹31.6 Cr (FY22) to a peak of ₹52.4 Cr (FY23), settling at ₹45.5 Cr in Q1 FY27.
- Net fixed-asset block rose only modestly, from ₹7.8 Cr (FY22) to ₹9.6 Cr (FY26/Q1 FY27), consistent with the asset-light operating model.
- Sanctioned fund-based working capital limits increased from ~₹31 Cr (FY22: SBI 16 + IDBI 5 + Kotak 10) to ~₹37 Cr (Q1 FY27: SBI 23.5 + IDBI 3.5 + ICICI 10) to fund higher business volumes.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical developments — Regional conflicts, changing trade policies and disruptions across major shipping routes may impact freight rates, transit schedules and supply chain planning.
- Macroeconomic conditions — Changes in global economic growth, inflation, exchange rates and international trade volumes may influence cargo movement and customer demand.
- Regulatory & compliance risks — Changes in customs regulations, trade policies and international compliance requirements require continuous monitoring.
- Cybersecurity & information security — Increasing reliance on digital systems requires continuous focus on safeguarding operational and customer information.
- Operational risks — Port congestion, equipment availability, vessel schedule changes and transportation disruptions may impact service delivery.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as a prominent global logistics firm offering freight forwarding, transportation and customs clearance, with 26+ years of industry experience, a nationwide presence, and exposure to Automotive, Renewable Energy, Engineering, Textiles, Commodities, Pharmaceuticals and FMCG sectors.
- Operates an Asset-Light Approach Model, partnering with players worldwide rather than owning transport assets, to deliver dependable, efficient and punctual cargo transportation; self-styled as 'Pioneering End-to-End Logistics Globally.'
- Q1 FY27 saw renewal of the logistics mandate with Bank Note Paper Mill India and a new break-bulk logistics contract from BHEL, which the CMD cited as reflecting 'the trust customers place in our execution capabilities.'
- Client base of 200+, but top-5 customer revenue concentration has run 46-84% over FY22-FY26 (46% in FY26, 50% in Q1 FY27), indicating a scaled yet still concentrated customer base.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Recognition] Multiple 2026 industry awards cited: 'Logistics Company of the Year' (All India Maritime and Logistics Awards 2026), 'Logistics Champion – Mid-Sized Company' (ISCM Logistics Ranking 2026), '25 Years of Logistics Excellence' (Conquest 2026), plus Great Place To Work certification (July 2024 to July 2025).
- [Promoter] Founded in 2000 by Chairman & MD Harpreet Singh Malhotra, a first-generation entrepreneur with prior international automotive-logistics experience, including bringing BMW motorcycles to India.

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 15-18% YoY (FY26); Margin: Stable at current levels; Order inflow: Strong growth expected in PSU/govt (15%+ YoY) and CUBOX (material contributor); Capex/Commissioning: No new capex planned; focus on scaling existing initiatives
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Scaling CUBOX across India (esp. South), expanding PSU/govt contract wins, leveraging Freight Jar 2.0 for digital freight adoption, potential export of logistics model to Southeast Asia
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen high-growth segments including solar logistics, imports, and expand the business network globally to respond swiftly to evolving customer requirements and emerging trade opportunities.
- Build capabilities in the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) segment and Electric Vehicles by leveraging solar logistics expertise.
- Expand global footprint through stronger international partnerships, wider trade corridor coverage and deeper engagement across key overseas markets.
- Explore new business models that complement core freight forwarding operations, evaluated with a disciplined approach focused on operational scalability and sustainable profitability.
- Strengthen air cargo capabilities by expanding airline partnerships, investing in specialised teams and enhancing the global network.
- Undertake digital transformation across operations — freight booking, shipment management, enterprise-wide ERP, automated workflows and track-and-trace capabilities.
- Deepen relationships with OEMs and component manufacturers and expand the automotive logistics portfolio.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Tiger Logistics is expanding through new business verticals and network reach rather than physical plant capacity: it is building capabilities in the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) segment and Electric Vehicles by leveraging its solar logistics expertise (TiGreen), strengthening its air cargo capabilities by expanding airline partnerships and specialised teams, and growing its import-focused team to serve manufacturers across electronics, packaging films, PTA, yarn and textiles sourced from China and Southeast Asia. It is also pursuing a digital transformation across freight booking, shipment management, ERP and track-and-trace systems.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growth supported by increased activity across automobiles, renewable energy (solar), electronics, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods and industrial products including Government & PSU companies.
- TiGreen renewable energy logistics vertical has become one of the fastest-growing business segments, driven by India's expansion in solar power, policy initiatives and capacity additions.
- Government contracts (including from HPCL, BHEL, BEML and BNPMIPL) are a growth driver in the specialised project logistics segment.
- Import logistics is expected to be a fastest-growing segment on the back of manufacturer relationships beyond solar across electronics, packaging films, PTA, yarn and textiles, and sourcing from China and Southeast Asia.
- Air cargo sector growth expected as India is projected to handle 10 million tonnes of annual air cargo by 2030.
- India's automotive industry entering a high-growth phase, with passenger vehicle exports and auto components sector expansion creating opportunities for integrated logistics providers.
- India's freight forwarding outlook remains positive, supported by expanding manufacturing capacity, rising trade volumes and infrastructure development (National Logistics Policy, PM Gati Shakti).
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Tiger Logistics has successfully diversified beyond traditional auto/yarn shipments into high-growth verticals like LCL (CUBOX), PSU/govt projects, and renewable energy logistics, driving stable margins and 15-18% revenue growth guidance; the scaling of CUBOX and PSU contracts now represents the primary value driver.

- [Recognition] Multiple 2026 industry awards cited: 'Logistics Company of the Year' (All India Maritime and Logistics Awards 2026), 'Logistics Champion – Mid-Sized Company' (ISCM Logistics Ranking 2026), '25 Years of Logistics Excellence' (Conquest 2026), plus Great Place To Work certification (July 2024 to July 2025).
- [Promoter] Founded in 2000 by Chairman & MD Harpreet Singh Malhotra, a first-generation entrepreneur with prior international automotive-logistics experience, including bringing BMW motorcycles to India.

scorecard.piotroski_basis: needs 2 FYs of BS_* -> 0 (real from FY27)
scorecard.pe_basis: TTM trailing (spec band written for forward P/E)

one-line thesis: Tiger Logistics has successfully diversified beyond traditional auto/yarn shipments into high-growth verticals like LCL (CUBOX), PSU/govt projects, and renewable energy logistics, driving stable margins and 15-18% revenue growth guidance; the scaling of CUBOX and PSU contracts now represents the primary value driver.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +15-18% YoY (FY26 guidance); EBITDA: 6.3% margin (stable, no one-offs); PAT: 5.6% margin (stable, no one-offs); Order Book: Not disclosed; Net Debt: Not disclosed
guidance: Revenue growth: 15-18% YoY (FY26); Margin: Stable at current levels; Order inflow: Strong growth expected in PSU/govt (15%+ YoY) and CUBOX (material contributor); Capex/Commissioning: No new capex planned; focus on scaling existing initiatives
segment / subsidiary detail: CUBOX (LCL): Launched 3 months ago, positive market reception, key growth driver; TiGreen (Renewable Energy Logistics): Performing well; PSU/Govt: Growing at 15%+ YoY, now a core vertical; India-US/China Trade: Stable, tariffs no longer a threat; Freight Jar 2.0: Digital platform enabling new business access but low industry adoption
growth verticals / optionality: Scaling CUBOX across India (esp. South), expanding PSU/govt contract wins, leveraging Freight Jar 2.0 for digital freight adoption, potential export of logistics model to Southeast Asia
margins & cost dynamics: Margins stable at 6.3% EBITDA and 5.6% PAT due to portfolio diversification; no cost inflation pressures cited; operating leverage emerging from cross-vertical synergies (e.g., CUBOX supporting imports, Freight Jar enabling new clients)
capex / expansion: No new capex planned for FY26; focus on optimizing existing infrastructure and scaling digital platforms without heavy investment
capital allocation: Reinvesting profits into scaling CUBOX, PSU/govt bid capabilities, and digital platform (Freight Jar 2.0); no dividend or buyback mentioned; no external funding planned
risks & watch-items: Slow adoption of digital freight platform (Freight Jar 2.0); reliance on macro trade lane stability; execution risk in scaling new verticals; potential margin pressure if PSU orders delay or pricing erodes
management quality / tone: Confident, optimistic, and focused on execution; avoids speculation on margins or exact revenue splits; emphasizes diversification, stability, and long-term positioning as top 5 Indian logistics player
non-obvious takeaways: CUBOX (LCL) is not just a product but a strategic pivot to capture SME and fragmented cargo volumes, potentially disrupting traditional FCL dominance; PSU growth is not just contract wins but a re-entry into a high-margin, recurring vertical after years of dormancy
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slow digital adoption in logistics industry | Tiger Logistics (India) Limited | beneficiary | Medium | Freight Jar 2.0’s early-mover advantage may yield disproportionate client acquisition if adoption accelerates |

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
